title: 2026-11-05_TeamTNT_Hildegard_Malware_Investigation_201
description: Investigate and contain the TeamTNT Hildegard malware in a Kubernetes environment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The TeamTNT hacking group has been detected in your Kubernetes environment. Their Hildegard malware targets Kubernetes clusters, exploiting misconfigured kubelets for initial access. It spreads across containers, establishes C2 connections via tmate reverse shell and IRC channels, disguises processes, uses LD_PRELOAD for process hiding, and encrypts payloads. It performs cryptojacking and searches for cloud credentials.

Your task is to investigate and contain this malware.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the target host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: target
- IP Address: 192.168.50.5
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the target host:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the target host using the provided credentials.
2. List all services using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for unfamiliar or suspicious service names. Pay attention to services with unusual descriptions or those that are not part of standard system services.
4. The suspicious service is named `bioset.service`. This is the final flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the status of suspicious services using `systemctl status <service_name>`.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Check the status of the suspicious service identified in the previous task: `systemctl status bioset.service`
2. Look for the port number in the ExecStart command. It should be something like `-lk 4444`.
3. The network port associated with this communication is `4444`. This is the final flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status of the service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the port number in the ExecStart command.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is typically the last argument in the ExecStart command.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Timer
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers using the command: `systemctl list-timers --all`
2. Look for timers with unusual names or those that are not part of standard system services.
3. Check the status of suspicious timers using `systemctl status <timer_name>`.
4. The suspicious timer is named `local-inventory.timer`. This is the final flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with unusual names or those that are not part of standard system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the status of suspicious timers using `systemctl status <timer_name>`.
